finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it. Any authenticated user can set privileged or server-controlled fields on their own record, such as role, isAdmin, id, email-verified flags, or tenant/org id. This allows privilege escalation or account/identity tampering. A `__proto__` key in a JSON body is a lesser concern, because Object.assign uses [[Set]] and JSON.parse creates an own `__proto__` property, which assign would then set on the target's prototype. That could change the prototype of req.user only.
finding.source: req.body (JSON) from any authenticated user, e.g. PUT /me {"role":"admin","isAdmin":true}
finding.sink: Object.assign(req.user, req.body) followed by req.store.save(req.user), which persists the attacker-chosen fields

trace.note: Route handler for PUT /me receives the attacker-controlled body
Object.assign merges all body keys into req.user with no allowlist
The modified user is persisted via the store
The full user object is returned, which confirms the change and may leak internal fields

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist, schema validation, or role check in this file. The sibling route /me/profile destructures only displayName and bio, which shows the intended safe pattern and that /me lacks it. Authentication middleware that sets req.user is not in this directory, so I could not check it. Even with authentication in place, the flaw is exploitable by any logged-in user.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, and users.js:6 persists it and users.js:7 returns it, so any authenticated user can set role or similar fields. The auth middleware and the store's save() are not in this directory, and the sibling route at users.js:11 shows the safe pattern is missing here.

verdict_facts.reason: users.js:5 does Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist or validation, and users.js:6 persists it. Any authenticated user can reach it, and the safe pattern at users.js:11-12 is not used here.
